body:
`find_λ_range` uses `floor(λ / 360)` in place of the hand-built floor division `ifelse((λ < 0) & (mod(λ, 360) != 0), λ ÷ 360 - 1, λ ÷ 360)`, so `interpolate!` compiles on Metal for Float32 `LatitudeLongitudeGrid`s.

On Julia ≥ 1.12, `÷` and `fld` on Float32 go through Float64 (JuliaGPU/Metal.jl#972), which Metal can't compile. The upstream fix, JuliaGPU/Metal.jl#975, needs Metal ≥ 1.10.1, which needs GPUCompiler 2, and Enzyme and Reactant cap it at 1.x. `floor(λ / 360)` matches `fld(λ, 360)` for every Float32 with 2.5e-43 < |λ| < 1.9e8 on the CPU.

- Adds a Metal test that interpolates between Float32 `LatitudeLongitudeGrid`s with longitudes (-180, 180) and (0, 360).
- A TODO at `find_λ_range` to switch to `fld` once Oceananigans can use a Metal release with the fix.

Closes #6056

Metal CI takes one `time_step!(model, 1.0)` for each of these combinations, which catches Float64 scalars leaking into kernels (see #5939, #6066):

- `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel`: `QuasiAdamsBashforth2`/`SplitRungeKutta3` × explicit/implicit (FFT)/split-explicit free surface × vertically implicit diffusion/CATKE
- `NonhydrostaticModel`: `QuasiAdamsBashforth2`/`RungeKutta3` with vertically implicit diffusion

Most of these configurations fail on main until #5940 is merged.

body:
As mentioned in #6125, some benchmarks were silently failing, and this was due to wrong interpolation of variables in Buildkite which requires double `$` to interpolate shell variables (as opposed to buildkite variables).

> Buildkite interpolates `$VAR` when it uploads the pipeline, so the single-`$` references to `GPU2_PID` and `GPU2_STATUS`, which are shell variables that only exist at run time, were replaced by empty strings. The script that actually ran was
> 
>     wait
>     GPU2_STATUS=$?
>     if [  -ne 0 ]; then
> 
> A bare `wait` returns 0 once all children have exited, and [the test errors out with `[: -ne: unary operator expected`](https://buildkite.com/clima/oceananigans-benchmarks-1/builds/10902#01a0dea1-4347-4ef6-bd3a-38263de439a2/L1276), so the warning could never fire and a crash in the background GPU 2 group went unreported. Build 10902 is an example: the Grid Type Sweep hit a `DomainError` in a CUDA kernel, the GPU 2 subshell stopped there (skipping the remaining Grid Type Sweep and the Tracer Count Sweep), and the step still passed.
> 
> Escape the references with `$$`, as already done for `$$!` and `$$?`. The step runs under `bash -e`, so a failing `wait $GPU2_PID` would abort the script before the status check and the merge of partial GPU 2 results. Capture the status with `wait ... || GPU2_STATUS=$?` instead, which keeps the intended behaviour: print the warning, merge whatever GPU 2 produced, and continue.
